items.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: then Eric Traub left and I asked if I could move to the tenor chair and he said no I want to keep you on bari.

ctx.x: I don’t try and just blow arbitrarily because I’m a cool jazz player and I can play outside so I’m going to play that way on her chart. If you hired me you hired me to play the way I play. I play the chart the way the chart feels, the era, writer, the mood, the vocalist, that’s the way you try and interpret a chart. That’s the important way to play. And so you draw on a lot from that. I mean I had all the years of listening to cats blow, Ben Webster, all the different guys. If you’re going to play the right way…

there Migs left — Migliore left, and I asked if I could move to the alto chair and he wanted me on bari so he said no, and then Eric Traub left and I asked if I could move to the tenor chair and he said no I want to keep you on bari. That was the last straw.
